hero: At the nurses' station of a bright freestanding hemodialysis unit in Malolos, Bulacan, a young Filipino resident physician in a white coat holds a pen above an open logbook while a Filipina unit manager stands beside him and dialysis chairs with patients are visible behind; morning light through windows, thoughtful mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Six separate systems each authorize one thing, and passing one check does not pass the others.
figures.content: Central icon of a dialysis unit building. Six labeled tiles around it, each with three short lines. 'PRC (RA 2382)': decides 'May you practice medicine?'; proof 'License and ID'. 'Training program': decides 'Your training status and supervised scope'; proof 'Appointment, training manual'. 'Hospital credentialing': decides 'Appointment and privileges here'; proof 'Privilege list'. 'DOH facility license (AO 2012-0001)': decides 'May the unit operate and who may staff it'; proof 'License to operate, roster'; small note 'POD ratio not more than 1:15'. 'PSN standards': decides 'Professional expectations for attending and POD'; proof 'Guidelines, POD course certificate'. 'PhilHealth': decides 'Accreditation and payment'; proof 'Accreditation, claim records'. Footer strip: 'One key does not open another door.'

figures.teaches: An adverse event moves from bedside safety to a system fix through six steps.
figures.content: Horizontal six-step flow with icons. 1 'Make safe' (treat, stop harm, call for help). 2 'Tell' (attending nephrologist, head nurse, patient and family). 3 'Record' (clinical note and adverse events logbook: facts and times, no blame). 4 'Review' (monthly CQI meeting led by the Dialysis Clinical Head: which condition allowed it?). 5 'Act and measure' (change one thing; track it on a run chart). 6 'Close the loop' (tell staff and patient what changed). A dashed return arrow from 6 to 1 labeled 'Fewer repeats'. Side box: 'PSN risk metrics: falls, needle injuries, medication errors, blood spills'.

card: An open logbook and a pen on a dialysis unit nurses' station counter, dialysis chairs softly blurred behind, no text.
